sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā ghorā rāghavāśramam āgatā rakṣasām ācacakṣe tau bhrātarau saha sītayā
english: Then the terrible Śūrpaṇakhā, having come to Rāghava's hermitage, described to the rākṣasas those two brothers together with Sītā.

sanskrit: te rāmaṃ parṇaśālāyām upaviṣṭaṃ mahābalam dadṛśuḥ sītayā sārdhaṃ vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca
english: They saw Rāma, of mighty strength, seated in the leaf-hut together with Vaidehī Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmān āgatāṃ tāṃ ca rākṣasīm abravīd bhrātaraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ dīptatejasaṃ
english: Seeing them — and the rākṣasī who had come — the glorious Rāghava spoke to his brother Lakṣmaṇa, blazing with energy.

sanskrit: muhūrtaṃ bhava saumitre sītāyāḥ pratyanantaraḥ imān asyā vadhiṣyāmi padavīm āgatān iha
english: "For a moment, O Saumitri, stand guard close beside Sītā — I shall slay these ones who have come here following her track."

sanskrit: vākyam etat tataḥ śrutvā rāmasya viditātmanaḥ tatheti lakṣmaṇo vākyaṃ rāmasya pratyapūjayat
english: Having heard this word of Rāma, who knows the self, Lakṣmaṇa honored Rāma's command with the reply: "So be it."

sanskrit: rāghavo 'pi mahac cāpaṃ cāmīkaravibhūṣitam cakāra sajyaṃ dharmātmā tāni rakṣāṃsi cābravīt
english: And Rāghava, the righteous one, strung his great bow adorned with gold, and then addressed those rākṣasas.

sanskrit: putrau daśarathasyāvāṃ bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau praviṣṭau sītayā sārdhaṃ duścaraṃ daṇḍakāvanam
english: "We two are sons of Daśaratha, brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa; we have entered the difficult Daṇḍaka forest together with Sītā."

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanau dāntau tāpasau dharmacāriṇau vasantau daṇḍakāraṇye kimartham upahiṃsatha
english: "Living on fruits and roots, self-restrained, ascetics who walk in dharma, dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest — why do you harm us?"

sanskrit: yuṣmān pāpātmakān hantuṃ viprakārān mahāvane ṛṣīṇāṃ tu niyogena prāpto 'haṃ saśarāsanaḥ
english: "I have come, bow in hand, by the command of the sages, to slay you wicked ones who commit outrages in the great forest."

sanskrit: tiṣṭhataivātra saṃtuṣṭā nopasarpitum arhatha yadi prāṇair ihārtho vo nivartadhvaṃ niśācarāḥ
english: "Stay right here, contented, and do not advance — if you value your lives, turn back, O night-roamers."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasās te caturdaśa ūcur vācaṃ susaṃkruddhā brahmaghnaḥ śūlapāṇayaḥ
english: Having heard his words, those fourteen rākṣasas — slayers of brāhmaṇas, tridents in hand — replied in great fury.

sanskrit: saṃraktanayanā ghorā rāmaṃ raktāntalocanam paruṣā madhurābhāṣaṃ hṛṣṭādṛṣṭaparākramam
english: With reddened eyes, those fierce ones addressed Rāma, whose eyes are red at the corners, who speaks sweetly though he addresses harsh things, whose prowess is gladly witnessed.

sanskrit: krodham utpādya no bhartuḥ kharasya sumahātmanaḥ tvam eva hāsyase prāṇān adyāsmābhir hato yudhi
english: "You have provoked the anger of our master, the great-souled Khara — you yourself shall lose your life today, slain by us in battle."

sanskrit: kā hi te śaktir ekasya bahūnāṃ raṇamūrdhani asmākam agrataḥ sthātuṃ kiṃ punar yoddhum āhave
english: "What power does one lone man have to stand before many of us at the forefront of battle — much less to fight us in combat?"

sanskrit: ebhir bāhuprayuktair naḥ parighaiḥ śūlapaṭṭiśaiḥ prāṇāṃs tyakṣyasi vīryaṃ ca dhanuś ca karapīḍitam
english: "By our iron clubs, tridents, and battle-axes, hurled by our arms, you shall forfeit your life, your valor, and the bow clutched in your hand."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā saṃrabdhā rākṣasās te caturdaśa udyatāyudhanistriṃśā rāmam evābhidudruvuḥ cikṣipus tāni śūlāni rāghavaṃ prati durjayam
english: Having spoken thus in fury, those fourteen rākṣasas, weapons and swords upraised, charged at Rāma alone — and hurled their spears at Rāghava, the unconquerable.

sanskrit: tāni śūlāni kākutsthaḥ samastāni caturdaśa tāvadbhir eva ciccheda śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: Kākutstha cut all those fourteen spears to pieces with exactly as many arrows adorned with gold.

sanskrit: tataḥ paścān mahātejā nārācān sūryasaṃnibhān jagrāha paramakruddhaś caturdaśa śilāśitān
english: Then, blazing with great energy and utterly enraged, he took up fourteen iron-shafted arrows, sun-bright and whetted on stone.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā dhanur āyamya lakṣyān uddiśya rākṣasān mumoca rāghavo bāṇān vajrān iva śatakratuḥ
english: Taking up his bow and drawing it to its full extent, aiming at his rākṣasa targets, Rāghava released those arrows like thunderbolts hurled by Śatakratu.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhāś ca viśikhāḥ pradīptā hemabhūṣaṇāḥ antarikṣe maholkānāṃ babhūvus tulyavarcasaḥ
english: Those sharp shafts with golden nocks, blazing and adorned with gold, blazed in the sky with the brilliance of great meteors.

sanskrit: te bhittvā rakṣasāṃ vegād vakṣāṃsi rudhirāplutāḥ viniṣpetus tadā bhūmau nyamajjantāśanisvanāḥ
english: Those arrows, drenched in blood, swiftly pierced through the rākṣasas' chests and drove into the ground with the sound of thunderbolts.

sanskrit: te bhinnahṛdayā bhūmau chinnamūlā iva drumāḥ nipetuḥ śoṇitārdrāṅgā vikṛtā vigatāsavaḥ
english: With their hearts split open, they fell to the ground like trees severed at the root — their limbs wet with blood, disfigured, their lives extinguished.

sanskrit: tān bhūmau patitān dṛṣṭvā rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā paritrastā punas tatra vyasṛjad bhairavaṃ ravam
english: Seeing them fallen on the ground, the rākṣasī, overcome with rage and terror, let out a dreadful cry.

sanskrit: sā nadantī mahānādaṃ javāc chūrpaṇakhā punaḥ upagamya kharaṃ sā tu kiṃ cit saṃśuṣka śoṇitā papāta punar evārtā saniryāseva vallarī
english: Śūrpaṇakhā, shrieking a great cry, swiftly went to Khara and, her blood somewhat dried, fell down again in anguish before him, like a creeper weeping its sap.

sanskrit: nipātitān prekṣya raṇe tu rākṣasān pradhāvitā śūrpaṇakhā punas tataḥ vadhaṃ ca teṣāṃ nikhilena rakṣasāṃ śaśaṃsa sarvaṃ bhaginī kharasya sā
english: Having seen the rākṣasas laid low in battle, Śūrpaṇakhā fled; the sister of Khara then reported fully and entirely the slaughter of all those rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa punaḥ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhāc chūrpaṇakhāṃ kharaḥ uvāca vyaktatā vācā tām anarthārtham āgatām
english: Seeing Śūrpaṇakhā fallen again, Khara spoke in anger with measured words to her who had come bringing news of calamity.

sanskrit: mayā tv idānīṃ śūrās te rākṣasā rudhirāśanāḥ tvatpriyārthaṃ vinirdiṣṭāḥ kimarthaṃ rudyate punaḥ
english: "I have just now dispatched those valiant rākṣasas, feeders on blood, for your sake — why do you weep again?"

sanskrit: bhaktāś caivānuraktāś ca hitāś ca mama nityaśaḥ ghnanto 'pi na nihantavyā na na kuryur vaco mama
english: "Devoted and loyal, ever well-disposed to me — even while slaying enemies they are not to be slain, for they would not disobey my word."

sanskrit: kim etac chrotum icchāmi kāraṇaṃ yatkṛte punaḥ hā nātheti vinardantī sarpavad veṣṭase kṣitau
english: "I wish to hear this — what is the cause for which you writhe on the ground again, crying out like a serpent, 'Ah, my master!'?"

sanskrit: anāthavad vilapasi kiṃ nu nāthe mayi sthite uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha mā bhaiṣīr vaiklavyaṃ tyajyatām iha
english: "Why do you lament as though without a protector when I, your protector, stand here? Rise up, rise up — do not fear; let this helplessness be abandoned."

sanskrit: ity evam uktā durdharṣā khareṇa parisāntvitā vimṛjya nayane sāsre kharaṃ bhrātaram abravīt
english: Thus addressed and fully consoled by the formidable Khara, she wiped her tear-filled eyes and spoke to her brother Khara.

sanskrit: preṣitāś ca tvayā śūrā rākṣasās te caturdaśa nihantuṃ rāghavaṃ ghorā matpriyārthaṃ salakṣmaṇam
english: "Those fourteen fierce and valiant rākṣasas were sent by you to slay Rāghava together with Lakṣmaṇa, for my sake."

sanskrit: te tu rāmeṇa sāmarṣāḥ śūlapaṭṭiśapāṇayaḥ samare nihatāḥ sarve sāyakair marmabhedibhiḥ
english: "But all of them — furious, tridents and battle-axes in hand — were slain in battle by Rāma with arrows that pierced their vital points."

sanskrit: tān bhūmau patitān dṛṣṭvā kṣaṇenaiva mahābalān rāmasya ca mahat karma mahāṃs trāso 'bhavan mama
english: "Seeing those mighty ones fallen to the ground in an instant, and witnessing Rāma's great feat, a tremendous terror seized me."

sanskrit: sāsmi bhītā samudvignā viṣaṇṇā ca niśācara śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ punaḥ prāptā sarvato bhayadarśinī
english: "I am afraid, deeply agitated, and dejected, O night-roamer — I have come again to you for refuge, seeing danger on every side."

sanskrit: viṣādanakrādhyuṣite paritrāsormimālini kiṃ māṃ na trāyase magnāṃ vipule śokasāgare
english: "Why do you not rescue me, sinking in the vast ocean of grief — haunted by crocodiles of despair, its waves a garland of terror?"

sanskrit: ete ca nihatā bhūmau rāmeṇa niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ye ca me padavīṃ prāptā rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ
english: "And these flesh-eating rākṣasas who came following my track have been slain on the ground by Rāma with sharpened arrows."

sanskrit: mayi te yady anukrośo yadi rakṣaḥsu teṣu ca rāmeṇa yadi śaktis te tejo vāsti niśācara daṇḍakāraṇyanilayaṃ jahi rākṣasakaṇṭakam
english: "If you have compassion for me and for those rākṣasas, if you have power and energy against Rāma, O night-roamer — then destroy this thorn of the rākṣasas who dwells in the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: yadi rāmaṃ mamāmitram adya tvaṃ na vadhiṣyasi tava caivāgrataḥ prāṇāṃs tyakṣyāmi nirapatrapā
english: "If you will not slay today this enemy of mine, Rāma, then I shall cast away my life right before your eyes, without shame."

sanskrit: buddhyāham anupaśyāmi na tvaṃ rāmasya saṃyuge sthātuṃ pratimukhe śaktaḥ sacāpasya mahāraṇe
english: "I consider with my mind and see that you are not capable of standing face to face in battle against bow-armed Rāma in great combat."

sanskrit: śūramānī na śūras tvaṃ mithyāropitavikramaḥ mānuṣau yan na śaknoṣi hantuṃ tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "You think yourself a hero but are no hero, your prowess is falsely claimed — for you cannot slay those two men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: apayāhi janasthānāt tvaritaḥ sahabāndhavaḥ niḥsattvasyālpavīryasya vāsas te kīdṛśas tv iha
english: "Leave Janasthāna quickly with your kinsmen — for one without substance and of little valor, what kind of dwelling is this place?"

sanskrit: rāmatejo'bhibhūto hi tvaṃ kṣipraṃ vinaśiṣyasi sa hi tejaḥsamāyukto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ bhrātā cāsya mahāvīryo yena cāsmi virūpitā
english: "Overwhelmed by the blazing power of Rāma, you will swiftly perish — for Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, is endowed with blazing power, as is his brother of mighty valor, by whom I was disfigured."

sanskrit: evam ādharṣitaḥ śūraḥ śūrpaṇakhyā kharas tadā uvāca rakṣasāṃ madhye kharaḥ kharataraṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus provoked by Śūrpaṇakhā, the valiant Khara then spoke, among the rākṣasas, words that were harsher than his name implied.

sanskrit: tavāpamānaprabhavaḥ krodho 'yam atulo mama na śakyate dhārayituṃ lavaṇāmbha ivotthitam
english: "This boundless wrath of mine born from your dishonor cannot be held back — like salt water risen in a flood."

sanskrit: na rāmaṃ gaṇaye vīryān mānuṣaṃ kṣīṇajīvitam ātmā duścaritaiḥ prāṇān hato yo 'dya vimokṣyati
english: "I do not count Rāma as formidable by his valor — he is a mere mortal whose life is exhausted; he has destroyed himself by his wicked deeds and today shall relinquish his life."

sanskrit: bāṣpaḥ saṃhriyatām eṣa saṃbhramaś ca vimucyatām ahaṃ rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā nayāmi yamasādanam
english: "Let these tears be checked and this agitation abandoned — I shall send Rāma together with his brother to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: paraśvadhahatasyādya mandaprāṇasya bhūtale rāmasya rudhiraṃ raktam uṣṇaṃ pāsyasi rākṣasi
english: "Today, O rākṣasī, you shall drink the warm blood of Rāma as he lies on the ground, his life barely remaining, struck down by my battle-axe."

sanskrit: sā prahṛṣṭvā vacaḥ śrutvā kharasya vadanāc cyutam praśaśaṃsa punar maurkhyād bhrātaraṃ rakṣasāṃ varam
english: She, delighted upon hearing the words that issued from Khara's mouth, foolishly praised her brother again as the best among rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tayā paruṣitaḥ pūrvaṃ punar eva praśaṃsitaḥ abravīd dūṣaṇaṃ nāma kharaḥ senāpatiṃ tadā
english: First rebuked by her and then praised again, Khara at that moment spoke to the army commander named Dūṣaṇa.

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi mama cittānuvartinām rakṣasīṃ bhīmavegānāṃ samareṣv anivartinām
english: "Fourteen thousand rākṣasas who follow my will, of terrible swiftness, who never retreat in battles —"

sanskrit: nīlajīmūtavarṇānāṃ ghorāṇāṃ krūrakarmaṇām lokasiṃhāvihārāṇāṃ balinām ugratejasām
english: "— dark as storm clouds in color, fierce, cruel in their deeds, who roam like lions among men, mighty, of terrible power —"

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śārdūladarpāṇāṃ mahāsyānāṃ mahaujasām sarvodyogam udīrṇānāṃ rakṣasāṃ saumya kāraya
english: "— of these rākṣasas, proud as tigers, with great gaping mouths, of mighty splendor, fully roused for every effort — have them marshaled, dear Dūṣaṇa."

sanskrit: upasthāpaya me kṣipraṃ rathaṃ saumya dhanūṃṣi ca śarāṃś ca citrān khaḍgāṃś ca śaktīś ca vividhāḥ śitāḥ
english: "Bring quickly for me, dear Dūṣaṇa, my chariot, bows, bright-colored arrows, swords, and diverse, sharpened lances."

sanskrit: agre niryātum icchāmi paulastyānāṃ mahātmanām vadhārthaṃ durvinītasya rāmasya raṇakovidaḥ
english: "I, skilled in battle, wish to march out at the fore, for the slaughter of that insolent Rāma on behalf of the great-souled descendants of Pulastya."

sanskrit: iti tasya bruvāṇasya sūryavarṇaṃ mahāratham sadaśvaiḥ śabalair yuktam ācacakṣe 'tha dūṣaṇaḥ
english: While he was yet speaking, Dūṣaṇa announced the great chariot, bright as the sun, yoked with excellent dappled horses.

sanskrit: taṃ meruśikharākāraṃ taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇam hemacakram asaṃbādhaṃ vaidūryamaya kūbaram
english: That chariot was shaped like the peak of Mount Meru, adorned with burnished gold, with golden wheels, unobstructed, with a pole inlaid with vaidūrya gems.

sanskrit: matsyaiḥ puṣpair drumaiś candrasūryaiś ca kāñcanaiḥ māṅgalyaiḥ pakṣisaṃghaiś ca tārābhiś ca samāvṛtam
english: It was adorned all over with auspicious images in gold: fish, flowers, trees, the moon and sun, flocks of birds, and stars.

sanskrit: dhvajanistriṃśasaṃpannaṃ kiṅkiṇīkavibhūṣitam sadaśvayuktaṃ so 'marṣād āruroha rathaṃ kharaḥ
english: Fitted with standards and swords, adorned with tinkling bells, yoked with fine horses — upon this chariot Khara mounted in fury.

sanskrit: niśāmya taṃ rathagataṃ rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ tasthuḥ saṃparivāryainaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Seeing him mounted on the chariot, the rākṣasas of terrible valor stood surrounding him, and surrounded the mighty Dūṣaṇa as well.

sanskrit: kharas tu tān maheṣvāsān ghoracarmāyudhadhvajān niryātety abravīd dṛṣṭvā rathasthaḥ sarvarākṣasān
english: Standing on his chariot, Khara looked upon all the rākṣasas — those great bowmen with their dreadful shields, weapons, and standards — and commanded: "March out!"

sanskrit: tatas tad rākṣasaṃ sainyaṃ ghoracarmāyudhadhvajam nirjagāma janasthānān mahānādaṃ mahājavam
english: Then that rākṣasa army — with dreadful shields, weapons, and standards — marched out from Janasthāna with a great roar and tremendous speed.

sanskrit: mudgaraiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiś ca paraśvadhaiḥ khaḍgaiś cakraiś ca hastasthair bhrājamānaiś ca tomaraiḥ
english: With clubs, battle-axes, very sharp tridents and hatchets, swords, and discuses held in hand, and gleaming javelins —

sanskrit: śaktibhiḥ patighair ghorair atimātraiś ca kārmukaiḥ gadāsimusalair vajrair gṛhītair bhīmadarśanaiḥ
english: — with lances, dreadful spiked clubs, oversized bows, maces, iron hammers, and thunderbolt-weapons grasped in their hands, terrible to behold —

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ sughorāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa niryātāni janasthānāt kharacittānuvartinām
english: — fourteen thousand of those most dreadful rākṣasas, followers of Khara's will, marched forth from Janasthāna.

sanskrit: tāṃs tv abhidravato dṛṣṭvā rākṣasān bhīmavikramān kharasyāpi rathaḥ kiṃ cij jagāma tadanantaram
english: Seeing those rākṣasas of terrible valor advancing, Khara's own chariot followed close behind them.

sanskrit: tatas tāñ śabalān aśvāṃs taptakāñcanabhūṣitān kharasya matam ājñāya sārathiḥ samacodayat
english: Then the charioteer, knowing Khara's intent, urged on those dappled horses adorned with burnished gold.

sanskrit: sa codito rathaḥ śīghraṃ kharasya ripughātinaḥ śabdenāpūrayām āsa diśaś ca pratiśas tathā
english: Urged on, that swift chariot of Khara — the slayer of foes — filled all the cardinal and intermediate directions with its sound.

sanskrit: pravṛddhamanyus tu kharaḥ kharasvano ripor vadhārthaṃ tvarito yathāntakaḥ acūcudat sārathim unnadan punar mahābalo megha ivāśmavarṣavān
english: The mighty Khara, whose voice is harsh, his fury grown great, roaring like a cloud raining hailstones, urged the charioteer on again, hastening like Death itself to slay his enemy.
